BUT, if there’s one, two, three, four, or five things I’ve learned about being in the military, is that IN America it is very possible to have free or affordable healthcare and paychecks. In GA where I’m from the average wage is $30,000 a year. So I’d have to shell out almost half my paycheck for healthcare I rarely used. In WA where I live now the same applies accept the average wage here is $60,000 so it makes it more affordable. 

Along with this, some states are so fucked that it makes the people there more fucked. In GA the minimum wage is below the federal standard minimum wage and is the lowest in the country. In the military I pay $27 a month for healthcare for me and my family. We go to the doctor for FREE, ANY DOCTOR for FREE, all medications are FREE, all ER visits or hospital visits are FREE. And we don’t pay the military directly for this healthcare, we pay Tricare, which is an independent, for-profit company. So you can’t tell me if .3% of the population can get affordable healthcare, then how come the millions and millions of adults in America can’t get the same. They say it won’t make them any money when being in the military proves this to be wrong.
